notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Nate Schmidt is on injured reserve and has missed the last 6 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
John Marino is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 14 games. He is a top-pair defenseman.
Nick Schmaltz is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-six forward.
Dylan Guenther is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-six forward. Clayton Keller has taken his spot beside Vincent Trocheck and Logan Cooley.
Quinn Hughes is day to day (upper-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Yakov Trenin is away for personal reasons and missed their last game. Nico Sturm has taken his spot beside Danila Yurov and Maxim Shabanov.
Olli Määttä is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin.
Marcus Foligno is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 10 games, down from 34% last season.

stakes: The Mammoth go in tied for fifth in the Central with 25 points, 13 points behind the Wild, first in the NHL.

MIN.head: A genuine toss-up
MIN.body: Utah has been out-chancing opponents lately, while Minnesota may be without Hughes. Then again, Minnesota has home-ice advantage, and Utah will be without Schmidt. The Wild can tip it if their power play gets going.

UTA.head: Too close to call
UTA.body: Utah has been out-chancing opponents lately, while Minnesota may be without Hughes. Then again, Minnesota has home-ice advantage, and Utah will be without Schmidt. The Mammoth can tip it if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: Sergachev fought last time
paras: The Wild won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Utah on Oct 27. The Wild have won five straight, and they’re rolling. The Mammoth (11-9-3) beat Colorado 4-1 on Nov 18. Going in, the Mammoth are fifth in the Central (tied for 15th in the NHL) and the Wild are first in the NHL.

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.543) says: their chances are worth about .706, and their goaltending has held them back. The Wild’s record (.792) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.636), largely thanks to their goaltending.
In their five-game winning streak, the Wild have outscored teams 24-9, including 16-7 at 5-on-5.

The Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st), let the point shots come and guard the net (1st) and get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (3rd). The Wild, by contrast, get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). They also draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.17 goals a game, the fewest in the league. Something has to give when the Wild’s shooting runs into the Mammoth’s defense. Beyond that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Clayton Keller (5 G / 24 A / 29 P in 23 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with eight goals in twelve games against Minnesota since 2023-24. Logan Cooley (11 G / 12 A / 23 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eleven goals. Kirill Kaprizov (18 G / 25 A / 43 P in 24 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is third in the NHL, with twelve points in his last five games.

Karel Vejmelka (6-7-2 / .869 SV% in 15 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Utah, but will likely start. Jesper Wallstedt (16-2-3 / .925 SV% in 21 GS) has been a rock in net for Minnesota and will likely start.

items.text: The Wild are newly without Quinn Hughes, Yakov Trenin and Olli Määttä, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche are missing more right now.
Last time these two met, there were three fights. For Mikhail Sergachev, it was his first fight since February 2023.

The Mammoth have been without Nate Schmidt, John Marino, Nick Schmaltz and Dylan Guenther for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche and the Wild are missing more right now.
Mikhail Sergachev has a point in six straight games against Minnesota, and 10 points in his last six against them.
